content: A benign pediatric heart murmur, also referred to as an innocent heart murmur, is a harmless sound that originates from the heart or the cardiovascular system and is detected during cardiac auscultation. By definition, an innocent murmur does not have any long-term impact on the health of the individual who has it. The characteristics of innocent murmurs include the following: They are soft in intensity, typically less than grade 3/6. They are often position-dependent, meaning they may vary when the child is lying down (supine) versus sitting or standing upright. The individual is otherwise healthy, with no concerns regarding growth or development. The murmur may be continuous (heard throughout the cardiac cycle) or systolic. It is important to note that murmurs heard only during diastole are always considered pathological. The second heart sound (S2) has normal splitting, which varies with inspiration. There is no palpable thrill, which refers to a vibration felt on the chest wall due to abnormal heart movement or blood flow. The prognosis for innocent murmurs is excellent. These murmurs are inconsequential and typically resolve as the child grows older. Additionally, diagnostic tests such as an electrocardiogram (ECG) and chest X-ray are normal in cases of innocent murmurs.
